statusDefinitions.verified: Every leaf in the workstream has executable boundary evidence and its relevant oracle or mutation can detect a broken implementation.
statusDefinitions.partial: Representative behavior is implemented and tested, but the workstream does not yet have leaf-complete boundary and mutation evidence.
statusDefinitions.unverified: The official clauses are inventoried, but no sufficient executable behavior evidence exists yet.

requirements: Every duel-applicable family is verified, not merely assigned to a family.
Every focused contract, runtime oracle, regression mutant, effect mutant, interaction scenario, fixed-seed fuzz run, and generated scenario passes.
The 40 other-mode leaves are either implemented or explicitly accepted as non-applicable to the two-player product scope.
Interactive choices, UI/server/AI legal actions, trajectory manifests, and the engine fingerprint pass the training-safety gate before any learning process starts.

verifiedMilestones.summary: Choices and later instructions remain inside the resolving Chain item; cleanup and nested triggers wait until the complete effect finishes.
evidenceTests: a choice in a multi-effect card explicitly continues the remaining effects before finishing the spell
triggers created during an effect wait until every instruction and draw has finished
lethal damage waits for every later instruction in the same Chain item

verifiedMilestones.summary: Combat roles affect current Might, lethal deaths are captured and moved in the official order, and combat healing/attacker recall occurs only at the inserted special-cleanup steps.
evidenceTests: cleanup assigns combat designations before lethal damage uses Shield Might
combat special cleanup heals an aura survivor before the next normal cleanup
simultaneous cleanup deaths are removed before other-unit death triggers are evaluated

verifiedMilestones.summary: Deathknell and later death-observer events retain separate batches; post-death triggers evaluate their source zone after simultaneous movement.
evidenceTests: a spell-killed Immortal Phoenix can trigger from trash after its simultaneous death
later other-unit death triggers resolve above an earlier Deathknell event
simultaneous cleanup deaths are removed before other-unit death triggers are evaluated

verifiedMilestones.summary: Direct Kill, prepared replacement payments, multiple Kill sequences, and Kill additional costs explicitly resume their owning operation.
evidenceTests: a direct Kill resumes its owning spell after an optional death replacement choice
a prepared death payment resumes the interrupted direct Kill exactly once
a replaced Kill additional cost remains paid and resumes the card-play process
a multi-Kill trigger resumes every remaining unit after a death replacement choice

verifiedMilestones.summary: An 'if this kills' follow-up is tied to the exact damage event and resolves only after cleanup confirms that event caused the death.
evidenceTests: Disintegrate draws only when its own damage event kills the unit

verifiedMilestones.summary: A Battlefield controller without a unit there loses Control only in an Open state without automatically awarding it to an occupant, and a Chain created only by a trigger does not incorrectly pass Focus when it empties.
evidenceTests: Open-state cleanup removes control when the controller has no unit without awarding it to an occupant
non-showdown chain gives Priority to the newest remaining item's controller
diana lunari showdown trigger can be declined
a Showdown Chain opened by a triggered ability does not pass Focus when it empties

evidenceTests: card categories follow the independent Neutral/Showdown Open/Closed permission matrix

direct and interactive card entry points share the Closed-state Reaction gate

a Hidden card gains its conditional Reaction permission beginning on the next turn
Check Legality rejects Ambush when its destination loses the friendly unit before Finalize

verifiedMilestones.summary: Every current card-level exception that grants Reaction timing—printed Reaction, Quick-Draw, a previously Hidden card, and destination-qualified Ambush—routes through one reviewed registry and shared engine gate; new exception kinds fail static validation until reviewed.
evidenceTests: registered play-timing exceptions route through one reviewed Reaction permission contract

verifiedMilestones.summary: Cards, activated abilities, and triggers reuse the one existing Chain; a Closed turn cannot create a sibling Showdown Chain, and simultaneous Chain representations are rejected by the runtime oracle.
evidenceTests: cards, abilities, and their triggers join the one existing Chain
a Unit creates its play trigger only after its Chain item resolves
showdown start choices resume remaining battlefield defend triggers
Core Rules runtime oracle rejects illegal zone, player, chain, attachment, and numeric states

verifiedMilestones.summary: Played tokens resolve immediately when finalized, ordinary Units and Gear wait for the Execute and Pass response window before resolving, and only actual Rune Pool Add abilities use the shared immediate-Finalize path without passing Priority or Focus; Channel abilities remain ordinary Chain items.
evidenceTests: Units and Gear remain finalized on the Chain until the Pass step resolves them
a Unit creates its play trigger only after its Chain item resolves
playing a token is a Unit play but not a card play
only Rune Pool Add effects use the immediate-Finalize ability classification
an Add Reaction finalizes during payment without passing Priority or Focus
malzahar fanatic pays its Kill cost and immediately finalizes the non-reactive Add ability

verifiedMilestones.summary: Neutral and Showdown Chains share one uninterrupted two-player Pass-cycle contract: adding any card, ability, or trigger clears earlier passes, fewer than two consecutive passes cannot resolve an Item, and exactly the newest Item resolves after both players pass.
evidenceTests: adding a Chain Item resets prior passes before the next Pass cycle
Neutral and Showdown Chains require one uninterrupted all-player Pass cycle per resolved Item
adding an Action Chain Item resets prior passes through the shared Pass-cycle contract

verifiedMilestones.summary: At both the first and later Execute windows, the Priority player may append only legally timed cards or abilities, retains Priority through the resulting Finalize pass, may append again before passing, and transfers Priority to the other duel player only by passing.
evidenceTests: cards and abilities use every first and later two-player Execute window through Finalize
card categories follow the independent Neutral/Showdown Open/Closed permission matrix
activated abilities follow the same independent state permission matrix as cards

verifiedMilestones.summary: The newest Item resolves in full, including explicit choice continuations; triggers created during Resolve remain on the same Chain and re-enter Finalize, while an emptied played-card Showdown Chain passes Focus and a nonempty Chain returns Priority to its newest remaining controller.
evidenceTests: a Pending trigger created during Resolve re-enters Finalize before the next Execute window
a choice in a multi-effect card explicitly continues the remaining effects before finishing the spell
triggers created during an effect wait until every instruction and draw has finished
Defy counters an eligible opposing spell on the chain
targeted spell does not retarget if declared unit leaves before resolution
a Showdown Chain opened by a played card passes Focus when it empties

verifiedMilestones.summary: Controlled opposing and uncontrolled Battlefield contests created by standard or effect movement stage the correct Combat or non-combat Showdown, and the player who applied Contested receives initial Focus and Priority; played-card Chains pass Focus on empty while trigger/Add-only Chains do not.
evidenceTests: standard and effect movement give Showdown Focus to the player who applied Contested
an Add ability that opens and empties its transient Showdown Chain does not pass Focus
a Showdown Chain opened by a triggered ability does not pass Focus when it empties
a Showdown Chain opened by a played card passes Focus when it empties

verifiedMilestones.summary: Cleanup, Start, Combat, and Ending Tasks retain an explicit owner while Chain work is produced; a Task incurred during Handle or any FEPR stage pauses and resumes that stage exactly once, and Pending Items created during Resolve restart FEPR at Finalize.
evidenceTests: turn tasks cannot pause without an explicit continuation owner
the independent HOT/FEPR model resumes every interrupted stage exactly once
Start and Ending Tasks survive Chain Pass, Resolve, and choice re-entry without skip or duplication
cleanup finishes hidden removal before resolving deathknell draw choices
combat special cleanup heals an aura survivor before the next normal cleanup
a Pending trigger created during Resolve re-enters Finalize before the next Execute window

verifiedMilestones.summary: The first empty Showdown Pass transfers Focus, the final uninterrupted Pass closes the Showdown into a Cleanup-owned exit Task, and only units surviving that Cleanup can proceed to Combat or establish Control and Conquer.
evidenceTests: card categories follow the independent Neutral/Showdown Open/Closed permission matrix
activated abilities follow the same independent state permission matrix as cards
Showdown exit Cleanup precedes Combat and Conquer settlement
combat showdown skips combat damage if the attacking side leaves after reactions
a battlefield can only score once for the same player each turn

verifiedMilestones.summary: Completed Pending Items finalize in append order without passing Priority; the Chain creator receives the first Execute window, and every later Execute window with items remaining belongs to the newest remaining Item's controller while Showdown Focus stays unchanged.
evidenceTests: Chain oracle rejects stable Pending Items and incorrect newest-controller Priority
Chain finalization and post-resolution Priority follow the independent FEPR model
ordinary activated abilities use the action Chain before resolving
showdown chain keeps Focus but gives Priority to the newest remaining item's controller

verifiedMilestones.summary: Action and Reaction timing on activated abilities does not turn the source card itself into an Action or Reaction card.
evidenceTests: activated ability timing keywords do not make their source cards Action or Reaction cards
ordinary Legend activated abilities use their controller's neutral open action timing
Action belongs to Malzahar's ability rather than the unit card

verifiedMilestones.summary: Awaken, Beginning, Hold, Channel, Draw, Rune Pool expiration, Ending effects, Ending Special Cleanup, and turn advancement execute in the official order and retain their process owner through Chain Pass, Resolve, and choice re-entry. Expiration-created FEPR repetition remains tracked in the turn/cleanup subledger.
evidenceTests: turn tasks cannot pause without an explicit continuation owner

verifiedMilestones.summary: Cleanup refreshes staged Showdowns and Combats from current occupancy, downgrades an invalid staged Combat when its Contested Showdown remains, lets the turn player order staged events, and upgrades an ongoing non-combat Showdown when opposition appears.
evidenceTests: turn player chooses the order when multiple combats are staged

verifiedMilestones.summary: A declared end turn remains pending while staged Showdowns or Combats are outstanding; the Ending Step, including Stunned expiration, begins only after those structured phases finish.
evidenceTests: cleanup downgrades an invalid staged combat to the remaining contested showdown before Ending

verifiedMilestones.summary: Cards and tokens complete distinct Played lifecycles; every card enters the one Chain as Pending, and cards played by a resolving effect wait until that effect and its Tasks finish before Finalize and response.
evidenceTests: cards and tokens follow the independent complete play lifecycle
playing a token is a Unit play but not a card play
a card played by a resolving effect waits for that effect and grants a new response window
